newsitem.title: MONACO: ATHLETICS-KOMEN ABANDONS 3,000 WORLD RECORD BID.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KOMEN ABANDONS 3,000 WORLD RECORD BID.

text.p: Kenya's 5,000 metres world champion Daniel Komen has decided to abandon a scheduled attempt to break his own 3,000 metres world record at the Monaco grand prix on Saturday but will take on several Olympic champions over 1,500 instead.

Meeting director Jean-Pierre Schoebel said on Friday that Komen had made the late change on the eve of the meeting because he was disappointed by his defeat by Haile Gebrselassie in Zurich on Wednesday when the Ethiopian smashed his own world 5,000 record.

It would have been a huge effort for Komen to break the 3,000 mark of seven minutes, 20.67 seconds he set in Rieti last season so soon after Zurich despite the fact that many of the fastest times in history in the non-championships distance have been set at this "Herculis" meeting.

The 21-year-old Komen admitted before the Zurich race that he would find it physically hard to break the 5,000 record just a few days after his triumph at the world championships in Athens last weekend.

In the 1,500 the Kenyan will now take on Algeria's reigning Olympic champion Noureddine Morceli and Spain's 1992 Olympic champion Fermin Cacho, the silver medallist at last year's Olympic Games in Atlanta.
Cacho broke Briton Steve Cram's 12-year-old European record when he finished second in Zurich in 3:28.95 in a fast race in Zurich.
Burundi's Venuste Niyongabo, the Olympic 5,000 champion, is also listed to compete at the distance.

But, although Komen has broken a world junior record at 1,500, the pressure on the Kenyan to produce a brilliant performance over the distance will not be as great as it would have been at 3,000 where he could have earned $50,000 for a world record.

Schoebel announced several late changes on Friday which have come as a result of a historic night in Zurich when world records tumbled in the men's 800 and 3,000 metres steeplechase as well as the 5,000.

In the 3,000 steeplechase world champion Wilson Boit Kipketer, who is not related to the 800 world record holder with a similar name, was due to take on compatriots Moses Kipatani and Bernard Barmasai who pulled him along to a world record of 7:59.08 seconds in Zurich.

But Kiptanui has decided he does not want the pressure of his new rival as he bids to retain the steeplechase record which he held before Kipketer's victory on Wednesday. Kipketer will now fill the gap left by Komen in the 3,000 flat.

Denmark's former Kenyan Wilson Kipketer, who took nearly half a second off Seb Coe's 16-year-old 800 world record on Wednesday -- the oldest record in the book -- with a time of one minute 41.24 seconds, also goes over two-laps in Monaco.
But he is unlikely to be able to lift himself again so soon after Zurich's performance when he ran an astonishing 48.10 seconds for the first 400 metres.
American world 100 metres champions Maurice Greene and Marion Jones are hoping to bounce back after defeats in Zurich.

Greene takes on former world record holder Leroy Burrell and American world bronze medallist Tim Montgomery in the men's 100. Namibia's Frankie Fredericks, who beat Greene in Zurich and was originally down to take him on again in Monaco, has switched to the 200 where he will face newly-crowned world champion Ato Boldon.
Jones runs the women's 200 against Ukraine's world champion Zhanna Pintusevich and Jamaican veteran Merlene Ottey who beat the American over 100 in Zurich.
